text: The KV cache stores key and value tensors for every token so attention is not recomputed each step. Its size grows linearly with sequence length and dominates GPU serving memory, capping how many requests fit concurrently.
Grouped-query attention shares key and value heads across query heads, shrinking the KV cache and raising serving throughput with little quality loss.
PagedAttention allocates the KV cache in fixed-size blocks like OS virtual memory, so only the last partial block is wasted. It is the change that most increased real-world LLM serving throughput.
Model cascading runs a cheap model first and escalates to a stronger model only when confidence is low, cutting cost while protecting quality on hard queries.
Retrieval-augmented generation grounds answers in retrieved documents, reducing hallucination and letting you update knowledge without retraining the model.
Hybrid retrieval fuses dense (semantic) and sparse (BM25 lexical) search with reciprocal rank fusion, catching both paraphrases and exact-term matches.
A semantic cache returns a stored answer when a new query is embedding-similar to a previous one, collapsing many paraphrases of the same question into one model call.
Input guardrails screen prompts for injection and PII before the model; output guardrails check toxicity and grounding before the response reaches the user.
Offline evaluation gates model and prompt changes on a versioned dataset, measuring faithfulness and task success with LLM-as-judge plus regression detection.
LoRA freezes the base model and trains small low-rank adapters, so hundreds of task-specific fine-tunes can share one base model at serving time.
